Just yesterday a friend of mine asked me if I thought we'd ever be able to travel through time. I said that, technically, we already are.

No, because of simple laws of chemistry and physics that would be broken with even a single time-travel journey. For instance, let's take the law of conservation of matter:

This natural law says that matter can neither be created nor destroyed. In the most simplistic way of explaining things, if you have an X amount of lead, you must end with an X amount of lead, since it can't be created on increase that amount above X nor destroyed to attain a value below X.

So, let's say we start off with 1kg of gold. We put it into a time machine, and send it ten minutes into the future. Well, for the next ten minutes, I have literally destroyed matter. One moment, the universe contains a specific amount of gold, and the next, it's 1kg less. This matter doesn't exist, anywhere at all.

Then, ten minutes later, the universe suddenly has an extra kilogram of gold that it didn't have to begin with. Now, we've literally created matter. We have made matter which wasn't there in the beginning. Even if you were to send it back in time, you have had an extra kilogram for some period of time, which violates the most basic universal law of the conservation of matter.

Then you run into the issues with physics and thermodynamics. Much like the conservation of matter, you have to conserve energy and entropy. Creating or destroying matter will either increase or decrease the total energy of the universe, which is impossible.

Similarly, it would create a discontinuous jump in the state variable we call entropy. In plain English, entropy can be graphed as a continuous, smooth graph. No jumps, no breaks, and no problems. Creating or destroying matter would create a sudden, discontinuous "jump" in this graph, which would ultimately mean you have a black hole where time, space, and matter no longer play by the rules of our universe.

This is one of my favorite questions to ponder and ponder I have. I believe it is possible to travel forward and backward in time.

Scenario #1 - Time Dilation One of the Apollo missions proved that traveling through space fast enough distorts time. By that I mean it makes time for the travelers pass at a slower speed than for non-travelers (Observers). What this means is that if you travel far enough and fast enough time slows down for you but not everyone else. Imagine you fly through space for 1 year at .5c (half the speed of light) and then return to Earth. By your clock 1 full year has passed. But back here on Earth 10 years have passed. So to an observer hear on Earth you would appear to have traveled INTO THE FUTURE.

 I believe that when we figure out how to travel faster than the speed of light we will actually be able to travel back in time. If my theory is correct you could leave Earth and travel at 1.5c (1.5 times the speed of light) for one year and when you returned to Earth it would be 10 years before you left.

Scenario #2 - Amplification of Time Travel I believe that it is possible to use a massive object like the Sun to amplify the Time Dilation referenced above. Imagine you fly around the Sun (repeatedly) at .5c for 1 year. Then return to Earth, instead of 10 years having passed on Earth from Scenario #1, this time 50 years have passed on Earth. By the same token if you traveled around the Sun at 1.5c for one year you would arrive back on Earth 50 years in the past.

Scenario #3 - Compressed Space One of the leading theories for Faster Than Light Travel is the idea you can fold space over on itself, thereby making hundreds of light years only a few thousand miles apart. I believe this is not only possible but would qualify as Time Travel because to an outside observer we would have traveled trillions of miles in a matter of minutes.

Scenario #4 - Black Hole Theory I believe if you where able to fly across the Event Horizon of a Black Hole at .5c with some kind of gravitational shielding to prevent you being sucked into the black hole that it would shoot you hundreds or even thousands of years into the future. At the same time I believe if you traveled across the Event Horizon of a Black Hole at 1.5c it would shoot you hundreds or even thousands of years into the past.

We are in fact traveling through time right now. You can increase or decrease the rate at which you travel forward, but you can't go backwards. It's like dividing by zero, it is just something that can't be done.
